item.title: [Recap] Davion Mitchell (MIA): Davion Mitchell posted a full line on Saturday with 15 points (4-of-7 FGs), four rebounds, nine assists, two steals, two blocks and three three-pointers against the Pistons.
item.description:
Davion Mitchell posted a full line on Saturday with 15 points (4-of-7 FGs), four rebounds, nine assists, two steals, two blocks and three three-pointers against the Pistons.

Fresh off dropping a career high 17 assists on Friday, Mitchell wasn’t able to record another double-double, but he came close. He ended up making up for it by contributing extra value on the defensive end in what has been arguably his best two-game stretch of the season. He has been one of the best late-round picks in fantasy basketball this season and should continue to stuff the stat sheet as Miami’s starting point guard for the rest of the season.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Giannis Antetokounmpo (MIA): Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Heat with 34 points (13-of-17 FGs), 14 rebounds, eight assists, one steal, three blocks and one three-pointer in a 137-117 win over the Pistons on Saturday.
item.description:
Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Heat with 34 points (13-of-17 FGs), 14 rebounds, eight assists, one steal, three blocks and one three-pointer in a 137-117 win over the Pistons on Saturday.

Giannis wasn’t able to match his season high of 37 points that he set on Friday, but he was able to score at least 30 points for a third straight game, which led to Miami’s fourth straight win. Detroit didn’t have much of an answer for him, which helped him add an efficient shooting night to a dominant stat line. Plus, he was able to have an effective night at the free throw line, which helped inflate his value.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Klay Thompson (MIA): Klay Thompson returned to the lineup on Saturday and contributed 26 points (10-of-17 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one block and six three-pointers against the Pistons.
item.description:
Klay Thompson returned to the lineup on Saturday and contributed 26 points (10-of-17 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one block and six three-pointers against the Pistons.

Following a one-game absence, Thompson was back in the starting unit for the Heat and had another strong outing. This was his second-highest scoring performance of the year, and he has really shrugged off a slow start. Over his last seven games, he has averaged 20.7 points and 5.1 triples per game while shooting 50 percent from the floor and 46.8 percent from deep. If he continues to shoot this well, Miami should keep winning more games.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Injury] Duncan Robinson (DET): Duncan Robinson finished with 10 points (3-of-8 FGs), one rebound, one assist and two three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday.
item.description:
Duncan Robinson finished with 10 points (3-of-8 FGs), one rebound, one assist and two three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday.

Robinson exited this game late in the second quarter due to thigh soreness and didn’t end up returning. Kevin Huerter replaced him to start the second half, and if Robinson remains out in San Antonio on Tuesday, Huerter would likely get the start. Robinson has been a big part of Detroit’s success this season, but Huerter is a solid replacement that has been on fire lately.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Cade Cunningham (DET): Cade Cunningham led the Pistons with 33 points (8-of-20 FGs, 14-of-14 FTs), five rebounds, eight assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in a 137-117 loss to the Heat on Saturday.
item.description:
Cade Cunningham led the Pistons with 33 points (8-of-20 FGs, 14-of-14 FTs), five rebounds, eight assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in a 137-117 loss to the Heat on Saturday.

It wasn’t a great encore after his performance on Thursday, but Cunningham still led the way for Detroit. 12 of his points came in the fourth quarter, though it wasn’t enough to complete a comeback. Cade has been effective from the free throw line all season, but he has been on fire lately. Over his last three games, he has shot 34-of-35 from the charity stripe. Unfortunately, he wasn’t quite as dominant as he was on Thursday. Still, Cade has been well worth the first-round pick.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Kevin Huerter (DET): Kevin Huerter provided a boost off the bench with 20 points (9-of-15 FGs), four rebounds, seven assists, one steal, three blocks and two three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday.
item.description:
Kevin Huerter provided a boost off the bench with 20 points (9-of-15 FGs), four rebounds, seven assists, one steal, three blocks and two three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday.

Huerter has been fantastic off the bench for Detroit lately, and he filled up the box score once again in this one. Over his last four games, he has averaged 16.8 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 1.3 steals, 2.3 blocks and 1.8 triples per game while shooting 54.2 percent from the floor. His role may continue to expand, as Duncan Robinson exited early with a thigh injury. If he ends up missing any time, Huerter would start in his place, just like he did in the second half of this game.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Day'Ron Sharpe (BKN): Day’Ron Sharpe posted a double-double on Saturday with 16 points (7-of-14 FGs), 11 rebounds, five assists and one steal against the Grizzlies.
item.description:
Day’Ron Sharpe posted a double-double on Saturday with 16 points (7-of-14 FGs), 11 rebounds, five assists and one steal against the Grizzlies.

Sharpe started the year off slow, but he’s really starting to show why he was one of the best late-round targets. This was his second double-double of the season, and while he didn’t do as much on the defensive end in this game compared to what he’s done in recent games, he continues to be one of the best passing bigs in the league. Over his last five games, Sharpe has averaged 7.4 assists per game. Combined with efficient shooting, solid rebounding and defensive production, Sharpe’s game is tailor-made for category leagues.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Julius Randle (BKN): Julius Randle led the Nets with 22 points (8-of-16 FGs), four rebounds, five assists, three steals and three three-pointers in a 129-110 loss to the Grizzlies on Saturday.
item.description:
Julius Randle led the Nets with 22 points (8-of-16 FGs), four rebounds, five assists, three steals and three three-pointers in a 129-110 loss to the Grizzlies on Saturday.

After three straight games scoring in the teens, Randle was finally able to get over the 20-point mark in this game. They needed his offense a little more than usual in this game with Michael Porter Jr. (personal) unavailable. It hasn’t been a great start to the season for Randle, but the volume will continue to be there for him. More nights like this one will help him improve his season-long numbers.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Noah Clowney (BKN): Noah Clowney started on Saturday and finished with 15 points (6-of-14 FGs), seven rebounds, three assists, three blocks and three three-pointers against the Grizzlies.
item.description:
Noah Clowney started on Saturday and finished with 15 points (6-of-14 FGs), seven rebounds, three assists, three blocks and three three-pointers against the Grizzlies.

With Michael Porter Jr. (personal) ruled out for this game late, Clowney ended up entering the starting unit. He took advantage of the opportunity and put together a solid stat line, complete with multiple blocks and triples. The Nets play again on Monday against the 76ers. If MPJ remains out, Clowney could be in line for another start and would have some streaming appeal.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Matas Buzelis (CHI): Matas Buzelis delivered 18 points (5-of-9 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), nine rebounds and two assists over 30 minutes to propel the Bulls to a 117-106 win over the Timberwolves on Saturday.
item.description:
Matas Buzelis delivered 18 points (5-of-9 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), nine rebounds and two assists over 30 minutes to propel the Bulls to a 117-106 win over the Timberwolves on Saturday.

Buzelis has gotten off to a rocky start overall this season, but he looked sharp in the early stages of this one, pouring in a game-high 14 points on 5-of-6 shooting, including 2-of-3 from beyond the arc, in the opening half. He cooled off considerably afterwards, notching just four points in the entire second half. Still, he managed to do enough as Chicago’s primary offensive creator in place of injured rookie sensation Caleb Wilson, who is set to miss 4-6 weeks with a fractured right hand, to power them to a much-needed road win. It’s hard to trust him for fantasy purposes given how up-and-down he’s been, but he should get plenty of scoring chances while Wilson is sidelined for at least the next month.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Jaron Pierre Jr. (NOP): Jaron Pierre Jr. provided a boost off the bench with 13 points (5-of-11 FGs), two rebounds, one steal, one block and two three-pointers against the Nuggets on Saturday.
item.description:
Jaron Pierre Jr. provided a boost off the bench with 13 points (5-of-11 FGs), two rebounds, one steal, one block and two three-pointers against the Nuggets on Saturday.

After scoring 23 points for the Pelicans G League affiliate earlier in the day, Pierre ended up scoring in double figures for the second time in one day in this game. The 58th pick this past summer, this was the first time Pierre has played outside of blowouts, so it was good to see him play well. However, he shouldn’t be considered more than a dynasty stash at this point.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Tyrese Proctor (CLE): Tyrese Proctor recorded a triple-double with a team-high 24 points (10-of-19 FGs), 11 rebounds and 10 assists to lead the Cavaliers to a 127-117 win over the Mavericks on Saturday.
item.description:
Tyrese Proctor recorded a triple-double with a team-high 24 points (10-of-19 FGs), 11 rebounds and 10 assists to lead the Cavaliers to a 127-117 win over the Mavericks on Saturday.

The Cavaliers were without their entire starting five on the second night of a back-to-back, with nationwide travel disruptions on Friday contributing to a lengthy list of absences. Donovan Mitchell (knee), James Harden (calf), Peyton Watson (hamstring) and Jarrett Allen (knee) were all ruled out, while Evan Mobley missed his second consecutive game due to a toe sprain he sustained earlier this week. Proctor stepped up to lead Cleveland to an unexpected win by shooting over 50 percent from the floor, including 4-of-13 from three-point range. It was his first career triple-double. He’s played over 22 minutes in five consecutive games and has topped 15 points in three straight during that span. Cleveland has a three-game week coming up with home matchups against the Bulls, Grizzlies and Pacers.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Kyrie Irving (DAL): Kyrie Irving amassed a team-high 34 points (11-of-25 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block over 37 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers.
item.description:
Kyrie Irving amassed a team-high 34 points (11-of-25 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block over 37 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers.

Irving was one of the few bright spots for Dallas in this one as they struggled to get anything going offensively until it was too late. The veteran point guard knocked down 7-of-16 from three-point range and fell just one point shy of matching his previous season-high, which he set earlier this week against the Pacers. He’s delivered second-round fantasy value this season, averaging 22.7 points, 3.5 rebounds, 4.4 assists, 1.3 steals and 0.5 blocks through 11 games. The Mavericks are back in action with a quick turnaround when they face the Celtics, another one of Irving’s former teams, on Sunday.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Thomas Bryant (CLE): Thomas Bryant piled up a season-high 19 points (7-of-12 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds and three assists over 27 minutes in Saturday’s win over the Mavericks.
item.description:
Thomas Bryant piled up a season-high 19 points (7-of-12 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds and three assists over 27 minutes in Saturday’s win over the Mavericks.

Bryant recorded a double-double after drawing the start at center with both Jarrett Allen (knee) and Evan Mobley (toe) both out of action. The 29-year-old big man has played sparingly this season, but could wind up seeing additional minutes off the bench if Mobley is out for an extended period. Cleveland has a three-game week coming up with home matchups against the Bulls, Grizzlies and Pacers.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Cooper Flagg (DAL): Cooper Flagg accumulated 18 points (6-of-19 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists and one block over 38 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers.
item.description:
Cooper Flagg accumulated 18 points (6-of-19 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists and one block over 38 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Cavaliers.

It was an extremely rare clunker for Flagg, who missed on all six of his attempts from three-point range and shot just 32 percent from the floor. He’s cobbled together a pair of lackluster performances following a season-high 43-point performance against the Pacers earlier this week. Despite the recent rough patch, he’s supplied first-round fantasy value as an all-around contributor this season, averaging 24.1 points, 7.0 rebounds, 6.4 assists, 2.0 steals and 0.8 blocks through 12 games. The Mavericks are back in action with a road tilt against the Celtics on Sunday.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Zion Williamson (NOP): Zion Williamson led the Pelicans with 24 points (9-of-16 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, two assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in a 116-108 loss to the Nuggets on Saturday.
item.description:
Zion Williamson led the Pelicans with 24 points (9-of-16 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, two assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in a 116-108 loss to the Nuggets on Saturday.

Zion has taken major strides this season, and it has helped in fantasy hoops. Unfortunately, this was the third game this season that he failed to record a steal, which has been a strength for him, and he had his worst night at the free throw line this season, though he has improved overall this year. He made up for it by matching his season high for both three-pointers and blocks. Despite the lack of team success, Zion continues to fill up the box score.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Yves Missi (NOP): Yves Missi returned to the lineup on Saturday and contributed three points (1-of-4 FGs, 1-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist and four blocks against the Nuggets.
item.description:
Yves Missi returned to the lineup on Saturday and contributed three points (1-of-4 FGs, 1-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist and four blocks against the Nuggets.

Outside of the blocks, it wasn’t a great performance in his first game back. However, he was on a restriction that limited him to 22 minutes, and it was his first game since Oct. 23, which was a game he played just nine minutes. Basically, comparing it to his monster season-opening performance isn’t fair. Still, he immediately started, and he should keep that role moving forward. Keep holding on, and he should get better as he logs more games.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Christian Braun (DEN): Christian Braun finished with 17 points (6-of-14 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist, four steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Pelicans on Saturday.
item.description:
Christian Braun finished with 17 points (6-of-14 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist, four steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Pelicans on Saturday.

After a rough 2025-26 campaign, Braun’s start to this season was rough. However, he has had some solid performances, and this was one of his best. His biggest improvement from last season has been on the defensive end, as he has been one of the best sources of steals so far this season. He hasn’t shot the ball as efficiently as he has in previous seasons, but he has made up for it on defense and will look to keep it going entering a four-game week.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Jamal Murray (DEN): Jamal Murray lit up the Pelicans with 23 points (9-of-16 FGs), seven rebounds, nine assists and two blocks on Saturday.
item.description:
Jamal Murray lit up the Pelicans with 23 points (9-of-16 FGs), seven rebounds, nine assists and two blocks on Saturday.

Murray has had an excellent season, but he has really picked things up over their last three games, averaging 30.3 points, 6.3 assists, 2.0 blocks and 3.0 triples per game while shooting 60.3 percent from the floor. He is averaging a block per game this season and has exactly two in three straight, but after averaging 0.4 swats per game last season, that mark will regress as the season continues. Still, it has been a fantastic start to the season for him, and with a four-game week coming up, he should continue to thrive for fantasy managers.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Nikola Jokić (DEN): Nikola Jokić led the Nuggets with 26 points (9-of-14 FGs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, three steals and one three-pointer in a 116-108 win over the Pelicans on Saturday.
item.description:
Nikola Jokić led the Nuggets with 26 points (9-of-14 FGs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, three steals and one three-pointer in a 116-108 win over the Pelicans on Saturday.

It was a slow start to the year for Jokić, but he is starting to pick things up, especially over the last three games, where he has averaged 26.0 points, 11.7 rebounds and 9.0 assists per game while shooting 58.8 percent from the floor. The main improvement has been in his shooting percentage, as he is still at 51 percent on the season, which is well below his mark in recent years. This was the third time they’ve played the Pelicans this season, and while they did win all three, this was the only game where Jokić didn’t finish with a triple-double. Unfortunately for fantasy managers, they don’t play New Orleans again until April.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (OKC): Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Friday’s loss to the Clippers with 40 points (15-of-26 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
item.description:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Friday’s loss to the Clippers with 40 points (15-of-26 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and two three-pointers.

Gilgeous-Alexander finished with his third 40-point game of the season, but he wishes he’d scored 42 instead of 40. The two-time MVP’s shot as time expired missed the mark, resulting in a 113-112 Clippers victory. After shooting a combined 17-of-42 in two losses to the Trail Blazers, Gilgeous-Alexander was much more efficient on Friday, shooting well over 50 percent from the field. He could be in for another big night to end the week, as the Thunder visit the Kings on Sunday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Trae Young (WAS): Trae Young led the Wizards with 37 points (8-of-23 FGs, 17-of-17 FTs), two rebounds, 14 assists and four three-pointers in a 144-140 loss to the Pistons in double overtime on Thursday.
item.description:
Trae Young led the Wizards with 37 points (8-of-23 FGs, 17-of-17 FTs), two rebounds, 14 assists and four three-pointers in a 144-140 loss to the Pistons in double overtime on Thursday.

A big fourth quarter led to Trae setting a new season high for scoring. In fact, this was his first 30-point, 10-assist game as a Wizard and the 92nd of his career, which ranks fifth in NBA history. Unfortunately, after scoring his 33rd point at the buzzer with an incredible three-pointer to force overtime, he shot 0-of-7 from the floor in overtime, with the four extra points coming at the free throw line. Still, it was an excellent night for him and was certainly his best performance as a Wizard. It is also worth noting that AJ Dybantsa, despite a rough night, hit a tough mid-range shot to force the second overtime, which was a fun moment for the rookie.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Alex Caruso (OKC): Alex Caruso accounted for 14 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, three steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Alex Caruso accounted for 14 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, three steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.

The Thunder didn’t have Ajay Mitchell for Wednesday’s game, opening a spot in the starting lineup for Caruso. He took advantage of the opportunity, shooting 4-of-5 from beyond the arc. Caruso’s 14 points were a new season high for him, as he totaled 17 points in the first four games he played upon returning from an ankle injury. If Mitchell remains out for Friday’s game against the Clippers, Caruso would be worth rostering in 14-team leagues and some 12-team leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Isaiah Hartenstein (OKC): Isaiah Hartenstein accumulated 20 points (10-of-14 FGs), 11 rebounds, six assists and two steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Isaiah Hartenstein accumulated 20 points (10-of-14 FGs), 11 rebounds, six assists and two steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.

After totaling 19 points in Oklahoma City’s first five games of November, Hartenstein recorded his first 20-point game of the season on Wednesday. The negative for iHart was the turnovers, of which he was responsible for six. A few of the turnovers were due to offensive fouls, so there isn’t much to worry about there. Rostered in 83 percent of Yahoo leagues, Hartenstein is providing top-100 fantasy value, slightly better than his ADP.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (OKC): Shai Gilgeous-Alexander produced 31 points (9-of-20 FGs, 13-of-14 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander produced 31 points (9-of-20 FGs, 13-of-14 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.

Gilgeous-Alexander has scored at least 30 points in six games this season. Unfortunately for him and the Thunder, the team’s lack of established scorers proved costly in both losses to the Trail Blazers. Five other Thunder players scored in double figures, with Isaiah Hartenstein’s 20 leading the way. The lack of creators who can take some of the pressure off of Gilgeous-Alexander was evident in both losses to the Trail Blazers. He’ll remain an elite fantasy option, but SGA’s ceiling may have taken a slight hit because a few of his teammates are injured.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jrue Holiday (POR): Jrue Holiday accumulated 19 points (5-of-12 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Jrue Holiday accumulated 19 points (5-of-12 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.

A double-digit scorer in seven straight games, Holiday provided solid fantasy value on Wednesday. In addition to the 19 points, he shot 5-of-8 from beyond the arc and recorded good numbers in assists and steals. Through 11 games, Holiday has been close to a top-100 fantasy player, something most managers did not expect before the season began.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Sidy Cissoko (POR): Sidy Cissoko produced 19 points (6-of-9 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Sidy Cissoko produced 19 points (6-of-9 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.

Replacing Scoot Henderson (5/2/2 with one three-pointer) in the starting lineup ahead of Tuesday’s win over the Thunder, Cissoko played well in both victories. The Trail Blazers wing totaled 36 points, five rebounds, three assists, one steal and seven three-pointers in Portland’s two-game sweep of Oklahoma City. While Cissoko isn’t a must-add player right now, he’s worth watching in deep leagues to see if the last two games were a fluke.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Damian Lillard (POR): Damian Lillard recorded 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Damian Lillard recorded 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.

While Lillard didn’t lead the way offensively for the Trail Blazers as he did in Wednesday’s win over Oklahoma City, the production remained solid. He’s scored at least 20 points in seven of Portland’s first 11 games, and Dame has started every game. As long as he stays healthy, Lillard should be able to deliver a top-100 season, if not more.

item.title: [Recap] Deni Avdija (POR): Deni Avdija tallied 28 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, four steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Deni Avdija tallied 28 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, four steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.

One night removed from scoring 24 points in a win over the Thunder, Avdija was just as productive in the rematch. The 28 points were the most he’s scored in a game since November 2, when the Trail Blazers forward hit that number in a win over the Nuggets. While there were questions before the season began about Portland’s offensive pecking order, there haven’t been any issues so far, even when the currently injured Ja Morant was healthy. That’s great for those who used a top-50 draft pick on Avdija.

Raphielle Johnson

item.description:
